title: Shareholder agreement disputes - the common drafting gaps
p1:
Most shareholder disputes don't start with bad relationships. They start with unclear agreements.

Many founders believe a shareholder agreement only needs to cover ownership percentages and investment amounts. The real problems often appear years later when decisions become difficult.
p2:
A surprising number of conflicts come from small drafting gaps: unclear exit rules, vague decision-making powers, missing protections for minority shareholders, or no plan for what happens if founders disagree.

A clause that seems unnecessary on day one can become the most important sentence in the agreement later.
p3:
A strong shareholder agreement is not just about recording who owns what. It creates a roadmap for difficult situations — like selling shares, resolving deadlocks, bringing in new investors, or handling a founder's departure.

The practical takeaway: review agreements based on future conflicts, not just current expectations. Clear terms today can prevent expensive disputes tomorrow.
